audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed between layers: content win[0], win[1], win[2] and win[5] all read Orianna while the matching phases[N].side read "Skill". The packet levelChart agrees with content on all four.
audit.why: Levels 1-3 are Orianna's — Galio is melee with a 275-range taunt, she pokes from 815 with a stacking passive, and his kit returns no health. Levels 4-5 even out once Shield of Durand (18s) and Justice Punch (11s) are both live. Level 6 goes back to her because Hero's Entrance is a 180-second roaming ultimate rather than a lane-kill button, so shoving and punishing the side he leaves is free.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side = Orianna at 6/10 and phases[5].side = Orianna; rows 3 and 4 already agreed as Skill and were left untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named no Galio spike and carried an unsourced magnitude ("Luden's makes Q-W a third of a health bar").
audit.why: His spikes are Justice Punch falling from 11s to 7s across ranks and Hero's Entrance at 180/160/140 with 4000-5500 range — a map spike, not a lane one.
audit.corrected: Spike line rebuilt on those two numbers, with the point that his 6 buys him the map rather than the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields credit Galio with healing or sustain: spikes[0].text ("Shield of Durand passive and Q's healing tick"), whys[1] ("faster than his sustain refills"), whys[3] ("Shield of Durand sustain"), content.early ("Winds of War heal give him sustain"), content.mid ("his sustain refills whatever you poke") and wants.foe[0] ("Sustain through poke with Shield of Durand and Q heal").
audit.why: Nothing in Galio's kit heals. Winds of War is a tornado that deals damage over time; Shield of Durand is a charged stance that ends in a taunt; neither the text nor the derived flags carry a heal. The whole 'do not try to out-poke his sustain' plan is built on an ability he does not have — and it is the opposite of the truth, because poke is exactly what works into him.
audit.corrected: Every sustain claim removed and replaced with the real reason to be careful: the 825-range Winds of War return trade and the 275-range taunt.
sources: champ-data/_kits/galio.json (no heal flag on any slot; Q and W text)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text and wants.you[2] say Justice Punch "can interrupt your ult".
audit.why: Command: Shockwave is a command to the Ball that resolves after a short delay — it carries no channel flag and the shockwave happens at the Ball, not at Orianna. A knockup can stop the cast; it cannot stop a Shockwave that has already been commanded. The actionable version is a distance instruction: cast from outside his 650.
audit.corrected: "knocks you up mid-cast, so cast from range and out of its 650" replaces the interrupt claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither of the two interactions flagged in _missing for this matchup appeared anywhere on the page.
audit.why: First, Colossal Smash makes his next basic attack an area hit every few seconds — the burst opens with an auto wind-up, not a visible cast, so the wind-up is the cue. Second, Orianna owns no Movement ability, so a 650-range Justice Punch closing on her has no kit answer at all — Flash is the only out, and it has to be held for the gap-close rather than spent on the damage.
audit.corrected: The auto tell written into breakdown.cooldowns; the no-dash point written into dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, dosFull[2].d invented a "fifteen-second" Justice Punch, and the packet reports zero sequencing cues on the matchup.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7 — never fifteen. Winds of War 11/10/9/8/7, Shield of Durand 18/17/16/15/14, Hero's Entrance 180/160/140; Command: Protect 9s, Command: Shockwave 110/95/80.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, report[9].t, ahead and the do's/don'ts.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t tells an Orianna facing Galio to "buy the stopwatch the moment Zed hits 6".
audit.why: Zed is not in this matchup — a template leak.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles, and dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d both explained Justice Punch under titles about ball placement and ult timing.
audit.why: Copy-paste bleed — "W the ground he must dash across" was explained with a farm-path trade rule.

notes: The big one: six separate fields told the reader Galio out-sustains poke and heals through chip — spikes[0].text even named "Q's healing tick". Nothing in his kit heals. Winds of War is a damage-over-time tornado and Shield of Durand is a charged stance ending in a taunt; galio.json carries no heal flag on any slot. This looks like leftover text from a much older version of the champion, and it is worse than a template because it tells the reader to abandon the plan (poking him) that actually works. All six fields rewritten. Second correction: two fields said Justice Punch "interrupts your ult" — Command: Shockwave is a command to the Ball with no channel flag, so a knockup can stop the cast but not a Shockwave already commanded; replaced with the distance instruction, which is what the reader can actually act on. Both _missing interactions added (Colossal Smash's auto tell, and the fact that Orianna owns no Movement ability so Flash is her only answer to a 650 gap-close). NOTE ON A FLAG I DID NOT USE: galio.json marks Justice Punch with "terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes", and the _missing rule fired on it as terrain-cuts-retreat — but Riot's text for the ability describes only a step-back charge and a knockup, no terrain. Per the brief I trusted the description and wrote the no-dash point without claiming a wall.
